registerOne takes 7 parameters — three of them bare callbacks (run, entrypointExists, vibeConfigText) plus a defaulted deps object — making the call site (registerMcpClients) and the function body hard to read and easy to miscall as the signature grows further. Collapsing the callback trio into deps (which already exists as a bag for this purpose) would remove the positional-callback pile-up.

vibeConfigHasServer (checked against vibe project/agents config text) and alreadyRegistered (checked against CLI stdout) both exist to answer the same question — 'is this MCP server already registered for this client' — from two different evidence sources, and registerOne calls both. If their notions of 'already registered' ever diverge, registerOne's branching on the two independently can produce an inconsistent outcome (e.g. reporting 'registered' while the config-text path says 'unchanged', or vice versa) instead of funneling through one shared predicate.
